label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
To: timeline
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: none

Spent the last two Saturdays redoing the electric in a buddy’s shed. Thought it was going to be a little cleanup job. That was a nice thought. Lasted about four minutes.

The shed was getting power from THREE orange extension cords plugged into each other, out a basement window, across the yard and under the deck. Apparently the plan was if the first cord couldn’t reach the fire, the other two would help.

Found a splice wrapped in duct tape. Not electrical tape. Duct tape. Somebody looked at exposed wiring and said this calls for the same stuff holding my shop vac together.

Then there was a 30 amp breaker feeding 14 gauge wire. Folks, putting a bigger breaker on undersized wire doesn’t give you more power. It lets the wire get hotter before anything shuts off. That’s not an upgrade.

One outlet was hooked up with speaker wire. I guess if you plugged a radio into it the music went both directions.

And my personal favorite: a regular outlet with a GFCI STICKER on it.

A sticker.

By that logic I’m putting a Corvette emblem on my truck tomorrow and seeing what happens on 51.

Ceiling fan box was hanging on by one drywall screw. One. That screw had more responsibility than anybody involved in the original installation.

There was also a mouse nest in a junction box. Mice were fine. Completely unbothered. Nicest tenants in the place, although I’d question their choice of contractor.

Then I opened the panel and inside the door, in Sharpie, it says:

SHED - DONT TOUCH - RON

Buddy’s wife is standing there, looks at it and goes, “Who’s Ron?”

Like I’d know. Like they issue us a directory at the union hall. Oh yeah, Ron, extension cord division, retired after the sticker incident.

Now before everybody starts, I don’t think whoever did this was some evil genius trying to burn a place down. Cheap and a little proud is usually all it takes. Something turns on, nothing trips, and a guy figures he did a good job. Then it stays that way for years because “it’s always worked.”

That’s the part I want people to hear underneath the jokes. Working is not the same as safe. A light coming on tells you the light came on. It doesn’t tell you whether a connection is heating up under the deck or whether the breaker can protect the wire.

These are the kinds of problems that start fires. In sheds, garages, and houses. And they don’t care whether you meant well or saved a couple hundred bucks.

It’s redone now. Proper buried feed, correctly sized wire and breaker, actual GFCI protection, proper boxes and outlets, and a fan supported like somebody might be standing under it. No sticker-based safety equipment.

Call a licensed electrician. Not your buddy whose qualifications are owning pliers and watching a guy on YouTube say “pretty simple.”

Ask questions. Get it checked. I’d rather explain why something needs fixed than hear afterward that somebody smelled burning and figured it was nothing.

Anyway, two Saturdays, two pizzas and a case of Yuengling later, the mice are the only ones disappointed with the renovation.

Ron, wherever you are, we touched it.
